newsitem.title: GERMANY: German draft share law -- supervisory boards.
newsitem.headline: German draft share law -- supervisory boards.

text.p: The German Justice Ministry on Tuesday released details of a new draft share law. The following is a summary of the sections of the draft referring to supervisory boards of German companies. The summary was provided by the ministry in German and translated by Reuters.

* Multiple mandates. The maximum permitted number (which can be held by one person) remains at 10 but mandates as chairman or deputy chairman of the supervisory board will be counted double when assessing this.
* Election proposal. When new supervisory board members are proposed to shareholders, details of their other legal mandates and their main professional activity should be given.
* Frequency of meetings. The number of compulsory annual meetings per year is increased from two to four for bourse-listed companies.

* Large, ritualised supervisory boards created in line with laws on worker participation should be cut back as a matter of principle to 12 members. Its statutes may of course provide for 16 or 20 members. Smaller bodies allow more effective operation with greater accountability.

* The commissioning of auditors is no longer to be issued by the management board, but by the supervisory board. This means the auditors should gain greater detachment from the management. The report should be given directly to the supervisory board for the attention of the chairman.
* The participation of the auditor in the balance sheet meeting of the supervisory board or a balance sheet committee becomes compulsory.
* The circulation of the auditors' report to all members of the supervisory board or members of a balance sheet committee becomes mandatory.
* The supervisory board must include in its report details of how often a full meeting of the supervisory board was held and how many committees have been created.

* The enforcement of damages claims against members of bodies, particularly supervisory board members, in the case of gross negligence is made much easier by reducing the level of shareholder support required to table such a motion to five percent of the total or a nominal share value of two million marks.
* Bourse-listed companies should detail the additional further supervisory board mandates and other comparable mandates of all members of their governing bodies in an annexe to the annual report.
